text:
olivia: Nightly canary flagged a tail-latency regression on the long-seq workload (seq_len ~12k). NSYS trace attached. We see a kernel switch around step ~220 -> a much slower matmul path, huge HBM bursts, and KV read latencies climb. Anyone on this?

mike: Saw it too. Pulled the nsys file: lots of small kernel launches and an increase in `matmul_fallback` calls around the same time. HBM bursts up to ~760GB/s for ~10-15ms. KV read p95 jumps from ~2ms to ~18ms.

priya: Can you paste the nsys timeline snippet or the sampler output? Also, did the batching heuristic emit an oversized microbatch at that moment? Our auto-grow can be aggressive when avg_seq fluctuates.

olivia: Pasting a reduced nsys timeline I clipped from the trace: 

```
NSYS TIMELINE (excerpt):
step=218 kernel=matmul_opt_v2   duration=1.7ms  queue=compute_0
step=219 kernel=matmul_opt_v2   duration=1.8ms
step=220 kernel=matmul_fallback duration=4.6ms  (sudden switch)
step=221 kernel=matmul_fallback duration=4.9ms
HBM burst: peak=740GB/s  window=12ms
KV read: p50=0.9ms p95=6.2ms -> 18.9ms concurrent with HBM burst
microbatch_count at window=48  (batching heuristic ramped up)
```

daniel: That switch at 220 looks like the selector tripped. Our kernel selector picks `matmul_opt_v2` only if alignment and tile-fit checks pass; otherwise it falls back. Could be a subtle alignment/stride change at long sequences. Also the higher microbatch count means more concurrent KV reads, causing thrash.

kai: Related note: recent change to `batching::auto_grow` removed a cap on microbatch_count when avg_seq > 4096. Combined with prefetch window size this can oversubscribe HBM.

mike: Quick repro command I used: `nsys profile -o /tmp/longseq -t cuda,cudnn python -m bench.run --seq 12000 --batch 8 --target-microbatch 32`  Reproduces the switch consistently in my env.

perf-bot: perf-bot: summary for trace 3127890123: 99p tail up 210ms -> 1600ms, HBM peak 765GB/s, KV cache miss rate x3. Attached flame and table.

priya: Proposed quick mitigations: 1) cap microbatch growth based on seq_len via mem-model; 2) add selector guard to avoid switching to fallback when HBM util > 60% for more than X ms; 3) reduce prefetch window jitter to avoid synchronized read storms.

mike: I experimented forcing kernel via env to confirm: `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=matmul_opt_v2` + microbatch cap -> rerun gives 99p ~270ms, HBM peak ~420GB/s, KV p95 ~2.1ms. So kernel choice + batching both matter.

olivia: I'll open a PR to: (A) enforce microbatch caps for seq > 8k, (B) add a selector bailout when HBM utility high, (C) add an integration test that simulates wide seq distribution to catch regressions. I'll also attach the nsys and perfetto links to the ticket.

daniel: For the KV layer: consider lowering prefetch window from 4 -> 2 for long sequences and add randomized jitter to prefetch offsets. That should reduce synchronous read storms and evictions.

kai: I'll add a guard in `auto_grow` that inspects runtime HBM util metric and anneals growth if util > 55% for last 50ms. Also add telemetry to surface `microbatch_count` spikes.

priya: Config snippet suggestion to land quickly (example):
```
runtime:
  batching:
    max_microbatch_per_seq:
      default: 32
      ">8192": 8
  prefetch:
    window: 2
    jitter_ms: 4
  kernel_selector:
    hbm_util_threshold_pct: 60
    holdoff_ms: 50
```

mike: I'll run the refactor branch through our nightly canary with the cap + selector guard and post numbers.

olivia: Perfetto flame for the affected window is uploaded to the ticket: https://perf.redwood/trace/3127890123  (contains stack, DMA stalls, and timeline). Note: DMA stall counters spike after the kernel fallback starts. Could be a PCIe or NVLink contention in the multi-GPU sharded run.

priya: Good call to check DMA stalls. If PCIe is saturated those KV reads will queue and cause the observed p95 spikes. Can someone run `nvidia-smi dmon` and `nvlink` counters during the repro?

mike: Will do and paste output. Also adding a microbench that exercises KV prefetch + long seq to the perf harness.

olivia: Thanks everyone. I'll file INFR-4123 with the trace, PR pointers, and the experimental numbers. Let's track here and close out after canary confirms fixes.

mike: :thumbsup:

priya: Thanks — will review the PR once up.

kai: I'll follow up on the auto_grow guard and add metric alerts.

perf-bot: perf-bot: linked ticket INFR-4123, added baseline comparison artifacts.
